harnesstap v1.6.3
Agent harness configuration toolkit for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other coding CLIs

USAGE
  harnesstap [options] [command]

OPTIONS
  -V, --version            output the version number
  -v, --verbose              show verbose error output
  --no-color               disable color output
  --no-interactive         disable interactive prompts
  -h, --help               display help for command

COMMAND GROUPS
  auth (a)           Authenticate with HarnessTap Cloud and manage cloud accounts
  config             Manage project profile config (apm.yml)
  environment (e)    Manage reusable environments and plugin environment cascade
  github             Authenticate with GitHub for private marketplace and repo reads
  harness (h)        Manage the registered harness set
  help               Core concepts and scenario playbooks
  lock               Read apm.lock.yaml and export inventory artifacts
  marketplace (mkt)  Manage plugin marketplace sources
  mcp                Discover and install MCP Registry servers
  migrate (m)        Export or import workspace, plugins, or resources for offline sharing
  notifications      List and mark plugin update notifications
  plugin (l)         Manage plugins (named bundles of resources that can be applied to a project)
  policy             Inspect executable-trust and apm-policy.yml decisions
  profile (p)        Manage profile plugins and global profile switching
  resource (r)       Manage resources (individual pieces of AI configuration like agents, skills, or instructions)

PROJECT
  add <source>           Add skills from a remote or local source
  apply [plugins]        Resolve a plugin's dependency graph and materialize it
  approve [PACKAGE_REF]  Approve executable primitives from dependency packages
  audit                  Scan a project for hidden Unicode, lockfile hashes, apm-policy.yml, and executable trust
  compile                Compile local .apm/ primitives into resolved target harness directories
  deny [PACKAGE_REF]     Deny executable primitives from dependency packages
  doctor                 Check Node, native modules, paths, and harness detection
  history [path]         List configuration snapshots for a project
  init                   Initialize the harnesstap database and config directory
  install                Onboard a project from apm.yml (same as apply with no plugin selector)
  mirror [path]          Rematerialize registered harness files from one on-disk harness (or plugin/AGENTS.md fallback)
  open [path]            Open a file or directory in your system editor
  pack                   Pack an apm.yml project into an Agent Plugins 1.0 bundle (plugin.json + primitives + apm.lock.yaml)
  revert [snapshot-id]   Revert a project or global apply snapshot
  scan [path]            Scan a project directory or plugin source and import configurations into the database
  status [path]          Show current project status and drift summary
  targets                Show which apply harness targets resolve for this project, and why
  use                    Switch to a project-configured profile and environment

USAGE
  ht apply [options] [plugins...]

Resolve a plugin's dependency graph and materialize it

ARGUMENTS
  [plugins]  Plugins to apply

EXAMPLES
  ht apply base
  ht apply base --harness claude-code
  ht apply work --global
  ht apply ./build/my-pkg
  ht apply base --format json
  ht apply base --on-conflict replace

OPTIONS
  --global                  Materialize into machine home instead of the project
  --project <path>          Project directory
  --harness <slugs>         Comma-separated harness slugs
  --all                     Install/apply every canonical HT-mapped target (not agent-skills)
  --dry-run                 Show what would be written
  --format <mode>           Output format: human or json
  --interactive             Prompt instead of relying on explicit flags
  --ignore-plugin-versions  Skip checking Claude plugin pins against installed versions
  --strict-plugin-versions  Fail apply (exit 2) if any pinned plugin violates its version constraint
  --sync-plugins            Refresh all pinned plugin resources from install trees before apply (unresolved plugins are synced by default)
  --on-conflict <policy>    What to do when it already exists: replace, skip, prompt or cancel. overwrite, ignore and fail are aliases. Non-interactive default: cancel
  --explain                 Print the resolution trail: selected versions with their constraints, and every resource decision
  --update                  Ignore apm.lock.yaml, re-resolve the dependency graph, and refresh file hashes
  --strict                  Fail apply when ${VAR} environment placeholders cannot be resolved
  --force                   Override critical hidden-Unicode findings and continue apply
  -y, --yes                 Install pinned marketplace plugins without a prompt
  --force-remove            Also remove managed files you changed and unmanaged files in the way

USAGE
  ht install [options]

Onboard a project from apm.yml (same as apply with no plugin selector)

Reads repo-root apm.yml, resolves dependencies.apm (including transitive dependencies.apm on fetched packages) / dependencies.mcp (including MCP Registry v0.1 identities such as io.github...), compiles local .apm/ primitives, writes apm.lock.yaml, and materializes resolved target harness directories. Registry strings are fetched from registry.modelcontextprotocol.io and converted to the same native MCP files HT already emits. Self-defined registry: false entries keep command/url as authored. --mcp <id> appends the identity to apm.yml then runs install; a failed install rolls the manifest write back. Target resolution: --target/--all/--harness, then targets: in apm.yml, then project/global harness preference, then filesystem auto-detect. Declared targets: win over preference and folder detection. Fails closed when no target can be resolved. Commit the lockfile plus generated harness output. Same project-scope flags as apply. Does not take a plugin selector or --global.

EXAMPLES
  ht install
  ht install --project .
  ht install --mcp io.github.github/github-mcp-server --target cursor
  ht install --target cursor,claude
  ht install --harness claude-code,cursor
  ht install --dry-run
  ht install --update

OPTIONS
  --project <path>          Project directory
  --harness <slugs>         Comma-separated harness slugs
  --all                     Install/apply every canonical HT-mapped target (not agent-skills)
  --dry-run                 Show what would be written
  --format <mode>           Output format: human or json
  --interactive             Prompt instead of relying on explicit flags
  --ignore-plugin-versions  Skip checking Claude plugin pins against installed versions
  --strict-plugin-versions  Fail apply (exit 2) if any pinned plugin violates its version constraint
  --sync-plugins            Refresh all pinned plugin resources from install trees before apply (unresolved plugins are synced by default)
  --on-conflict <policy>    What to do when it already exists: replace, skip, prompt or cancel. overwrite, ignore and fail are aliases. Non-interactive default: cancel
  --explain                 Print the resolution trail: selected versions with their constraints, and every resource decision
  --update                  Ignore apm.lock.yaml, re-resolve the dependency graph, and refresh file hashes
  --strict                  Fail apply when ${VAR} environment placeholders cannot be resolved
  --force                   Override critical hidden-Unicode findings and continue apply
  -y, --yes                 Install pinned marketplace plugins without a prompt
  --force-remove            Also remove managed files you changed and unmanaged files in the way
  --mcp <id>                Append an MCP Registry v0.1 identity to apm.yml dependencies.mcp, then install

USAGE
  ht approve [options] [PACKAGE_REF...]

Approve executable primitives from dependency packages

Writes project apm.yml executables.allow by default. --user writes ~/.harnesstap/config.jsonc (can only narrow past org/project deny). --pending lists gated packages; --all approves them; --recommended accepts the org recommend set; --list shows the effective decision per locked package.

ARGUMENTS
  [PACKAGE_REF]  Packages to approve (owner/repo)

EXAMPLES
  ht approve owner/repo
  ht approve --user owner/repo
  ht approve --pending
  ht approve --all

OPTIONS
  --project <path>  Project directory
  --user            Write ~/.harnesstap/config.jsonc instead of apm.yml
  --pending         List packages with unapproved executables
  --all             Approve all currently pending packages
  --recommended     Approve the org executables.recommend set
  --list            Show effective trust decision per installed package
  --format <mode>   Output format: human or json

USAGE
  ht compile [options]

Compile local .apm/ primitives into resolved target harness directories

Same overlay path as ht install / ht apply with no plugin selector: existing writers, apm.lock.yaml local_deployed_file_hashes, policy, and trust. Resolution order: --target / --all / --harness, then targets: in apm.yml, then project/global harness preference, then filesystem auto-detect. Declared targets: win over preference so install stays portable. Fails closed when no target resolves. Does not take a plugin selector or --global. compilation.strategy: distributed is noted and ignored; output stays single-file root context (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md).

EXAMPLES
  ht compile
  ht compile --target cursor
  ht compile -t claude,cursor --dry-run
  ht compile --all
  ht compile --project . --format json

OPTIONS
  --project <path>          Project directory
  --harness <slugs>         Comma-separated harness slugs
  --all                     Install/apply every canonical HT-mapped target (not agent-skills)
  --dry-run                 Show what would be written
  --format <mode>           Output format: human or json
  --interactive             Prompt instead of relying on explicit flags
  --ignore-plugin-versions  Skip checking Claude plugin pins against installed versions
  --strict-plugin-versions  Fail apply (exit 2) if any pinned plugin violates its version constraint
  --sync-plugins            Refresh all pinned plugin resources from install trees before apply (unresolved plugins are synced by default)
  --on-conflict <policy>    What to do when it already exists: replace, skip, prompt or cancel. overwrite, ignore and fail are aliases. Non-interactive default: cancel
  --explain                 Print the resolution trail: selected versions with their constraints, and every resource decision
  --update                  Ignore apm.lock.yaml, re-resolve the dependency graph, and refresh file hashes
  --strict                  Fail apply when ${VAR} environment placeholders cannot be resolved
  --force                   Override critical hidden-Unicode findings and continue apply
  -y, --yes                 Install pinned marketplace plugins without a prompt
  --force-remove            Also remove managed files you changed and unmanaged files in the way

USAGE
  ht harness sync [options]

Union resources from registered harnesses and materialize with last-write conflicts

Scans every registered harness, unions portable types (skills, MCP, rules, host plugin install trees, and other serializer-supported resources), keeps the newest on-disk copy when the same identity differs (later registered harness on ties), and emits shared skill paths when multiple targets can read them. Claude and Cursor plugin trees are copied into each native root (they do not share a runtime plugin directory). Skills, agents, and commands inside those plugins are also materialized into `.agents` (and equivalent folders) for OpenCode and other harnesses that do not load Cursor/Claude plugin roots. Matching CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md share one file: AGENTS.md is canonical and CLAUDE.md links to it unless copy mode is set. Configure with `harnessSync.pluginResources` in config.jsonc (`symlink`, `copy`, or `clone`) or `--plugin-resources`. Default scope is the home directory. This is not copy-from-one-harness mirror.

EXAMPLES
  ht harness sync
  ht harness sync --dry-run --format json
  ht harness sync --plugin-resources copy
  ht harness sync --project .

OPTIONS
  --project <path>           Sync a git-backed project instead of home
  --dry-run                  Show what would be written without writing files
  --plugin-resources <mode>  How to materialize Cursor/Claude plugin files into .agents: symlink, copy, or clone (default symlink, or harnessSync.pluginResources in config.jsonc)
  --format <mode>            Output format: human or json

Scans every registered harness, unions portable types (skills, MCP, rules, host plugin install trees, and other serializer-supported resources), keeps the newest on-disk copy when the same identity differs (later registered harness on ties), and emits shared skill paths when multiple targets can read them. Claude and Cursor plugin trees are copied into each native root (they do not share a runtime plugin directory). Skills, agents, and commands inside those plugins are also materialized into `.agents` (and equivalent folders) for OpenCode and other harnesses that do not load Cursor/Claude plugin roots. Matching CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md share one file: AGENTS.md is canonical and CLAUDE.md links to it unless copy mode is set. Configure with `harnessSync.pluginResources` in config.jsonc (`symlink`, `copy`, or `clone`) or `--plugin-resources`. Default scope is the home directory. This is not copy-from-one-harness mirror.

EXAMPLES
  ht harness sync
  ht harness sync --dry-run --format json
  ht harness sync --plugin-resources copy
  ht harness sync --project .

OPTIONS
  --project <path>           Sync a git-backed project instead of home
  --dry-run                  Show what would be written without writing files
  --plugin-resources <mode>  How to materialize Cursor/Claude plugin files into .agents: symlink, copy, or clone (default symlink, or harnessSync.pluginResources in config.jsonc)
  --format <mode>            Output format: human or json

USAGE
  ht lock export [options]

Export a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM inventory from the existing lockfile (no re-resolve)

Inventory export only: reads apm.lock.yaml and serializes it. Never re-resolves, re-hashes, or touches the network. Default format is CycloneDX 1.5; --format spdx writes SPDX 2.3. This is not a security attestation: the document is unsigned and does not claim SLSA. --timestamp pins the document time; otherwise SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, then the lockfile generated_at. Diagnostics go to stderr so stdout stays pipe-clean.

EXAMPLES
  ht lock export
  ht lock export --format cyclonedx -o sbom.json
  ht lock export --format spdx --timestamp 2024-06-01T00:00:00+00:00
  ht lock export --project .

OPTIONS
  -f, --format <format>  SBOM output format: cyclonedx (1.5) or spdx (2.3)

  -g, --global           Read apm.lock.yaml from ~/.harnesstap/
  --timestamp <ts>       Pin the SBOM timestamp (timezone-aware ISO 8601) for reproducible output

SCENARIO 8: AUDIT PLUGIN RESOURCES AND PLUGIN PINS

Occasional · Shipped

  Use this when you want to understand which plugin resources are in the local
  library, which plugin pins a plugin carries, and whether installed plugin trees
  are still in sync with HarnessTap.
  There are two related surfaces:
  **Library plugin resources**: what HarnessTap knows about installed plugins:
  ```bash
  harnesstap resource list --type plugin_pin_pin
  harnesstap resource show formatter@team-marketplace
  harnesstap resource sync --dry-run
  harnesstap resource sync formatter@team-marketplace --overwrite
  ```
  `resource sync` refreshes marketplace-linked plugin resources from install
  trees under `~/.claude/plugins`, `~/.cursor/plugins`, and similar locations.
  Stale rows are reported when the install path cannot be resolved.
  **Plugin pins**: what a plugin expects at apply time:
  ```bash
  harnesstap plugin show my-setup
  harnesstap plugin doctor my-setup --check plugin-metadata
  harnesstap apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions
  ```
  Use **library sync** when chasing *"is this plugin resource up to date?"* and
  **plugin pins + apply validation** when chasing *"does this project satisfy the
  plugin's plugin constraints?"*. See Scenario 18 for debugging when committed
  project settings and effective Claude plugin loads disagree.

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht resource list --type plugin_pin_pin
  ht resource show formatter@team-marketplace
  ht resource sync --dry-run
  ht resource sync formatter@team-marketplace --overwrite
  ht plugin show my-setup
  ht plugin doctor my-setup --check plugin-metadata
  ht apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions

Full doc: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/08-audit-plugins.md
All scenarios: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/scenarios.md

SCENARIO 16: ENFORCE PLUGIN AND PLUGIN STATE IN CI

  Use this when you want CI to fail if the project drifts away from its plugin
  or its pinned plugin versions.
  Typical commands (each exits non-zero on a problem):
  ```bash
  harnesstap status . --check --format json
  harnesstap plugin doctor my-setup --format json
  harnesstap apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions --format json
  harnesstap resource sync --format json --dry-run
  harnesstap audit --ci --format json
  ```
  When `executables:` is opted in, `--ci` also fails on `required-executable-untrusted`. Approve with `ht approve <ref>` or inspect with `ht policy explain <ref>`.
  This pairs naturally with Scenario 12. The `--dry-run` keeps CI from writing
  files, while `--strict-plugin-versions` forces failure (exit 2) on a pin
  violation. Use `status --check` exit code 1 as the "working tree changed
  since last apply/sync" signal, and `plugin doctor` exit code 1 as the "plugin
  definition is invalid" signal.

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht status . --check --format json
  ht plugin doctor my-setup --format json
  ht apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions --format json
  ht resource sync --format json --dry-run
  ht audit --ci --format json

Full doc: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/16-ci-enforcement.md
All scenarios: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/scenarios.md

SCENARIO 17: MIGRATE HARNESSTAP STATE TO A NEW MACHINE

Rare · Shipped (manual workflow: see Scenario 28 (https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/28-machine-migration.md) for one-command migration)

  Use this when moving setups across laptops or onto a dev box. For a single
  archive that includes harness preferences and config, prefer Scenario 28 (https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/28-machine-migration.md).
  Manual workflow with current commands:
  ```bash
  # On the old machine
  mkdir -p ./bundles
  for p in $(harnesstap plugin list --format json | jq -r '.[].name'); do
  harnesstap migrate export "./bundles/$p" --plugin "$p" --embed-plugins
  done
  # Copy ./bundles/ to the new machine, then:
  harnesstap init
  for d in ./bundles/*/; do
  harnesstap migrate import "$d"
  done
  harnesstap harness set --main claude-code --aliases cursor,codex   # restore selection
  ```
  `--embed-plugins` is recommended for portability so the new machine does not
  need to re-fetch marketplace plugin trees. This workflow does not currently
  carry over harness preferences or `~/.harnesstap/config.json`; copy those by
  hand or use Scenario 28 (https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/28-machine-migration.md).

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht mkdir -p ./bundles
  ht for p in $(harnesstap plugin list --format json | jq -r '.[].name'); do
  ht migrate export "./bundles/$p" --plugin "$p" --embed-plugins
  ht done
  ht init
  ht for d in ./bundles/*/; do
  ht migrate import "$d"
  ht done
  ht harness set --main claude-code --aliases cursor,codex   # restore selection

SCENARIO 39: MCP AUTH, ENVIRONMENTS, AND ACCOUNT SWITCHING

Occasional · Documented

  Use this when you need to switch Slack workspaces, API tokens, or deployment
  targets across profiles/plugins: or when OAuth MCP servers do not respond after
  an environment switch.
  ## Quick decision
  | You have... | HarnessTap can... |
  | --- | --- |
  | Bot token / PAT in MCP `env` or `headers` | Switch via `environment use` + re-apply |
  | OAuth MCP (browser login in Cursor/Claude) | **Not** switch sessions: re-auth in the host app |
  Full reference: **Environments: MCP authentication limitations**
  ## Static token workflow (supported)
  ```bash
  # Seed from plugin MCP env keys
  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  # Switch and materialize
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  # or: ht apply my-setup --project . --harness claude-code,cursor
  ```
  Plugin MCP definitions should use placeholders, not literals:
  ```json
  "env": { "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN": "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" }
  ```
  Verify resolved keys before apply:
  ```bash
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run
  ```
  ## OAuth MCP (host-managed)
  After apply, open the target harness and complete OAuth there (Cursor MCP panel,
  `claude mcp`, Copilot `/mcp auth`, etc.). HarnessTap only writes server URL /
  transport: not OAuth tokens.
  ## Known gaps
  - **Shipped:** Cursor MCP scan/emit and HTTP `headers` round-trip (via `mcp-config-bridge`).
  - **OAuth sessions:** Browser OAuth tokens remain host-managed: environment switch does not re-auth for you.
  Remaining limitations: Known gaps and fix plan.
  Related: Portability limits,

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run

Full doc: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/39-mcp-auth-and-environments.md
All scenarios: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/scenarios.md

SCENARIO 8: AUDIT PLUGIN RESOURCES AND PLUGIN PINS

Occasional · Shipped

  Use this when you want to understand which plugin resources are in the local
  library, which plugin pins a plugin carries, and whether installed plugin trees
  are still in sync with HarnessTap.
  There are two related surfaces:
  **Library plugin resources**: what HarnessTap knows about installed plugins:
  ```bash
  harnesstap resource list --type plugin_pin_pin
  harnesstap resource show formatter@team-marketplace
  harnesstap resource sync --dry-run
  harnesstap resource sync formatter@team-marketplace --overwrite
  ```
  `resource sync` refreshes marketplace-linked plugin resources from install
  trees under `~/.claude/plugins`, `~/.cursor/plugins`, and similar locations.
  Stale rows are reported when the install path cannot be resolved.
  **Plugin pins**: what a plugin expects at apply time:
  ```bash
  harnesstap plugin show my-setup
  harnesstap plugin doctor my-setup --check plugin-metadata
  harnesstap apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions
  ```
  Use **library sync** when chasing *"is this plugin resource up to date?"* and
  **plugin pins + apply validation** when chasing *"does this project satisfy the
  plugin's plugin constraints?"*. See Scenario 18 for debugging when committed
  project settings and effective Claude plugin loads disagree.

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht resource list --type plugin_pin_pin
  ht resource show formatter@team-marketplace
  ht resource sync --dry-run
  ht resource sync formatter@team-marketplace --overwrite
  ht plugin show my-setup
  ht plugin doctor my-setup --check plugin-metadata
  ht apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions

SCENARIO 39: MCP AUTH, ENVIRONMENTS, AND ACCOUNT SWITCHING

Occasional · Documented

  Use this when you need to switch Slack workspaces, API tokens, or deployment
  targets across profiles/plugins: or when OAuth MCP servers do not respond after
  an environment switch.
  ## Quick decision
  | You have... | HarnessTap can... |
  | --- | --- |
  | Bot token / PAT in MCP `env` or `headers` | Switch via `environment use` + re-apply |
  | OAuth MCP (browser login in Cursor/Claude) | **Not** switch sessions: re-auth in the host app |
  Full reference: **Environments: MCP authentication limitations**
  ## Static token workflow (supported)
  ```bash
  # Seed from plugin MCP env keys
  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  # Switch and materialize
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  # or: ht apply my-setup --project . --harness claude-code,cursor
  ```
  Plugin MCP definitions should use placeholders, not literals:
  ```json
  "env": { "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN": "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" }
  ```
  Verify resolved keys before apply:
  ```bash
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run
  ```
  ## OAuth MCP (host-managed)
  After apply, open the target harness and complete OAuth there (Cursor MCP panel,
  `claude mcp`, Copilot `/mcp auth`, etc.). HarnessTap only writes server URL /
  transport: not OAuth tokens.
  ## Known gaps
  - **Shipped:** Cursor MCP scan/emit and HTTP `headers` round-trip (via `mcp-config-bridge`).
  - **OAuth sessions:** Browser OAuth tokens remain host-managed: environment switch does not re-auth for you.
  Remaining limitations: Known gaps and fix plan.
  Related: Portability limits,

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run

SCENARIO 8: AUDIT PLUGIN RESOURCES AND PLUGIN PINS

Occasional · Shipped

  Use this when you want to understand which plugin resources are in the local
  library, which plugin pins a plugin carries, and whether installed plugin trees
  are still in sync with HarnessTap.
  There are two related surfaces:
  **Library plugin resources**: what HarnessTap knows about installed plugins:
  ```bash
  harnesstap resource list --type plugin_pin_pin
  harnesstap resource show formatter@team-marketplace
  harnesstap resource sync --dry-run
  harnesstap resource sync formatter@team-marketplace --overwrite
  ```
  `resource sync` refreshes marketplace-linked plugin resources from install
  trees under `~/.claude/plugins`, `~/.cursor/plugins`, and similar locations.
  Stale rows are reported when the install path cannot be resolved.
  **Plugin pins**: what a plugin expects at apply time:
  ```bash
  harnesstap plugin show my-setup
  harnesstap plugin doctor my-setup --check plugin-metadata
  harnesstap apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions
  ```
  Use **library sync** when chasing *"is this plugin resource up to date?"* and
  **plugin pins + apply validation** when chasing *"does this project satisfy the
  plugin's plugin constraints?"*. See Scenario 18 for debugging when committed
  project settings and effective Claude plugin loads disagree.

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht resource list --type plugin_pin_pin
  ht resource show formatter@team-marketplace
  ht resource sync --dry-run
  ht resource sync formatter@team-marketplace --overwrite
  ht plugin show my-setup
  ht plugin doctor my-setup --check plugin-metadata
  ht apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions

Full doc: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/08-audit-plugins.md
All scenarios: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/scenarios.md

SCENARIO 16: ENFORCE PLUGIN AND PLUGIN STATE IN CI

  Use this when you want CI to fail if the project drifts away from its plugin
  or its pinned plugin versions.
  Typical commands (each exits non-zero on a problem):
  ```bash
  harnesstap status . --check --format json
  harnesstap plugin doctor my-setup --format json
  harnesstap apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions --format json
  harnesstap resource sync --format json --dry-run
  harnesstap audit --ci --format json
  ```
  When `executables:` is opted in, `--ci` also fails on `required-executable-untrusted`. Approve with `ht approve <ref>` or inspect with `ht policy explain <ref>`.
  This pairs naturally with Scenario 12. The `--dry-run` keeps CI from writing
  files, while `--strict-plugin-versions` forces failure (exit 2) on a pin
  violation. Use `status --check` exit code 1 as the "working tree changed
  since last apply/sync" signal, and `plugin doctor` exit code 1 as the "plugin
  definition is invalid" signal.

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht status . --check --format json
  ht plugin doctor my-setup --format json
  ht apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions --format json
  ht resource sync --format json --dry-run
  ht audit --ci --format json

Full doc: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/16-ci-enforcement.md
All scenarios: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/scenarios.md

SCENARIO 17: MIGRATE HARNESSTAP STATE TO A NEW MACHINE

Rare · Shipped (manual workflow: see Scenario 28 (https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/28-machine-migration.md) for one-command migration)

  Use this when moving setups across laptops or onto a dev box. For a single
  archive that includes harness preferences and config, prefer Scenario 28 (https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/28-machine-migration.md).
  Manual workflow with current commands:
  ```bash
  # On the old machine
  mkdir -p ./bundles
  for p in $(harnesstap plugin list --format json | jq -r '.[].name'); do
  harnesstap migrate export "./bundles/$p" --plugin "$p" --embed-plugins
  done
  # Copy ./bundles/ to the new machine, then:
  harnesstap init
  for d in ./bundles/*/; do
  harnesstap migrate import "$d"
  done
  harnesstap harness set --main claude-code --aliases cursor,codex   # restore selection
  ```
  `--embed-plugins` is recommended for portability so the new machine does not
  need to re-fetch marketplace plugin trees. This workflow does not currently
  carry over harness preferences or `~/.harnesstap/config.json`; copy those by
  hand or use Scenario 28 (https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/28-machine-migration.md).

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht mkdir -p ./bundles
  ht for p in $(harnesstap plugin list --format json | jq -r '.[].name'); do
  ht migrate export "./bundles/$p" --plugin "$p" --embed-plugins
  ht done
  ht init
  ht for d in ./bundles/*/; do
  ht migrate import "$d"
  ht done
  ht harness set --main claude-code --aliases cursor,codex   # restore selection

  Start with the full reference:
  **Portability limits**
  Quick checklist:
  ```bash
  # See what HarnessTap can import from a dual-mode repo
  harnesstap scan . --dry-run
  # Preview what each harness would receive
  harnesstap apply my-setup --project . --harness claude-code,codex,windsurf,opencode --dry-run
  # Check mirror warnings for harness-specific surfaces
  harnesstap mirror . --dry-run --format json
  # List harness capabilities (use --supported for natively serialized hosts only)
  harnesstap harness list --format json
  ```
  **Fully bridgeable:** skills, instructions, rules, MCP (stdio/http), static
  commands (md/toml), agents.

  plugin install), Copilot namespaced commands.
  **Harness-specific (mirror warnings):** OpenCode `.mjs` server plugins, pi
  extensions, Gemini extension manifests, statusline hooks, runtime session config.
  **Workarounds:** plugin pins + `resource sync`, automatic dual-mode scan,
  mirror `--reference auto|plugin`, and native `copilot plugin install` for Copilot
  plugin trees.

SCENARIO 39: MCP AUTH, ENVIRONMENTS, AND ACCOUNT SWITCHING

Occasional · Documented

  Use this when you need to switch Slack workspaces, API tokens, or deployment
  targets across profiles/plugins: or when OAuth MCP servers do not respond after
  an environment switch.
  ## Quick decision
  | You have... | HarnessTap can... |
  | --- | --- |
  | Bot token / PAT in MCP `env` or `headers` | Switch via `environment use` + re-apply |
  | OAuth MCP (browser login in Cursor/Claude) | **Not** switch sessions: re-auth in the host app |
  Full reference: **Environments: MCP authentication limitations**
  ## Static token workflow (supported)
  ```bash
  # Seed from plugin MCP env keys
  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  # Switch and materialize
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  # or: ht apply my-setup --project . --harness claude-code,cursor
  ```
  Plugin MCP definitions should use placeholders, not literals:
  ```json
  "env": { "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN": "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" }
  ```
  Verify resolved keys before apply:
  ```bash
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run
  ```
  ## OAuth MCP (host-managed)
  After apply, open the target harness and complete OAuth there (Cursor MCP panel,
  `claude mcp`, Copilot `/mcp auth`, etc.). HarnessTap only writes server URL /
  transport: not OAuth tokens.
  ## Known gaps
  - **Shipped:** Cursor MCP scan/emit and HTTP `headers` round-trip (via `mcp-config-bridge`).
  - **OAuth sessions:** Browser OAuth tokens remain host-managed: environment switch does not re-auth for you.
  Remaining limitations: Known gaps and fix plan.
  Related: Portability limits,

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run

Full doc: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/39-mcp-auth-and-environments.md
All scenarios: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/scenarios.md

SCENARIO 39: MCP AUTH, ENVIRONMENTS, AND ACCOUNT SWITCHING

Occasional · Documented

  Use this when you need to switch Slack workspaces, API tokens, or deployment
  targets across profiles/plugins: or when OAuth MCP servers do not respond after
  an environment switch.
  ## Quick decision
  | You have... | HarnessTap can... |
  | --- | --- |
  | Bot token / PAT in MCP `env` or `headers` | Switch via `environment use` + re-apply |
  | OAuth MCP (browser login in Cursor/Claude) | **Not** switch sessions: re-auth in the host app |
  Full reference: **Environments: MCP authentication limitations**
  ## Static token workflow (supported)
  ```bash
  # Seed from plugin MCP env keys
  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  # Switch and materialize
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  # or: ht apply my-setup --project . --harness claude-code,cursor
  ```
  Plugin MCP definitions should use placeholders, not literals:
  ```json
  "env": { "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN": "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" }
  ```
  Verify resolved keys before apply:
  ```bash
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run
  ```
  ## OAuth MCP (host-managed)
  After apply, open the target harness and complete OAuth there (Cursor MCP panel,
  `claude mcp`, Copilot `/mcp auth`, etc.). HarnessTap only writes server URL /
  transport: not OAuth tokens.
  ## Known gaps
  - **Shipped:** Cursor MCP scan/emit and HTTP `headers` round-trip (via `mcp-config-bridge`).
  - **OAuth sessions:** Browser OAuth tokens remain host-managed: environment switch does not re-auth for you.
  Remaining limitations: Known gaps and fix plan.
  Related: Portability limits,

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run

Full doc: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/39-mcp-auth-and-environments.md
All scenarios: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/scenarios.md

SCENARIO 8: AUDIT PLUGIN RESOURCES AND PLUGIN PINS

Occasional · Shipped

  Use this when you want to understand which plugin resources are in the local
  library, which plugin pins a plugin carries, and whether installed plugin trees
  are still in sync with HarnessTap.
  There are two related surfaces:
  **Library plugin resources**: what HarnessTap knows about installed plugins:
  ```bash
  harnesstap resource list --type plugin_pin_pin
  harnesstap resource show formatter@team-marketplace
  harnesstap resource sync --dry-run
  harnesstap resource sync formatter@team-marketplace --overwrite
  ```
  `resource sync` refreshes marketplace-linked plugin resources from install
  trees under `~/.claude/plugins`, `~/.cursor/plugins`, and similar locations.
  Stale rows are reported when the install path cannot be resolved.
  **Plugin pins**: what a plugin expects at apply time:
  ```bash
  harnesstap plugin show my-setup
  harnesstap plugin doctor my-setup --check plugin-metadata
  harnesstap apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions
  ```
  Use **library sync** when chasing *"is this plugin resource up to date?"* and
  **plugin pins + apply validation** when chasing *"does this project satisfy the
  plugin's plugin constraints?"*. See Scenario 18 for debugging when committed
  project settings and effective Claude plugin loads disagree.

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht resource list --type plugin_pin_pin
  ht resource show formatter@team-marketplace
  ht resource sync --dry-run
  ht resource sync formatter@team-marketplace --overwrite

  Use this when you want CI to fail if the project drifts away from its plugin

  ```bash

  harnesstap apply my-setup --project . --dry-run --strict-plugin-versions --format json
  harnesstap resource sync --format json --dry-run

  When `executables:` is opted in, `--ci` also fails on `required-executable-untrusted`. Approve with `ht approve <ref>` or inspect with `ht policy explain <ref>`.

  files, while `--strict-plugin-versions` forces failure (exit 2) on a pin
  violation. Use `status --check` exit code 1 as the "working tree changed
  since last apply/sync" signal, and `plugin doctor` exit code 1 as the "plugin
  definition is invalid" signal.

SCENARIO 39: MCP AUTH, ENVIRONMENTS, AND ACCOUNT SWITCHING

Occasional · Documented

  Use this when you need to switch Slack workspaces, API tokens, or deployment
  targets across profiles/plugins: or when OAuth MCP servers do not respond after
  an environment switch.
  ## Quick decision
  | You have... | HarnessTap can... |
  | --- | --- |
  | Bot token / PAT in MCP `env` or `headers` | Switch via `environment use` + re-apply |
  | OAuth MCP (browser login in Cursor/Claude) | **Not** switch sessions: re-auth in the host app |
  Full reference: **Environments: MCP authentication limitations**
  ## Static token workflow (supported)
  ```bash
  # Seed from plugin MCP env keys
  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  # Switch and materialize
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  # or: ht apply my-setup --project . --harness claude-code,cursor
  ```
  Plugin MCP definitions should use placeholders, not literals:
  ```json
  "env": { "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN": "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" }
  ```
  Verify resolved keys before apply:
  ```bash
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run
  ```
  ## OAuth MCP (host-managed)
  After apply, open the target harness and complete OAuth there (Cursor MCP panel,
  `claude mcp`, Copilot `/mcp auth`, etc.). HarnessTap only writes server URL /
  transport: not OAuth tokens.
  ## Known gaps
  - **Shipped:** Cursor MCP scan/emit and HTTP `headers` round-trip (via `mcp-config-bridge`).
  - **OAuth sessions:** Browser OAuth tokens remain host-managed: environment switch does not re-auth for you.
  Remaining limitations: Known gaps and fix plan.
  Related: Portability limits,

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run

Full doc: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/39-mcp-auth-and-environments.md
All scenarios: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/scenarios.md

SCENARIO 39: MCP AUTH, ENVIRONMENTS, AND ACCOUNT SWITCHING

Occasional · Documented

  Use this when you need to switch Slack workspaces, API tokens, or deployment
  targets across profiles/plugins: or when OAuth MCP servers do not respond after
  an environment switch.
  ## Quick decision
  | You have... | HarnessTap can... |
  | --- | --- |
  | Bot token / PAT in MCP `env` or `headers` | Switch via `environment use` + re-apply |
  | OAuth MCP (browser login in Cursor/Claude) | **Not** switch sessions: re-auth in the host app |
  Full reference: **Environments: MCP authentication limitations**
  ## Static token workflow (supported)
  ```bash
  # Seed from plugin MCP env keys
  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  # Switch and materialize
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  # or: ht apply my-setup --project . --harness claude-code,cursor
  ```
  Plugin MCP definitions should use placeholders, not literals:
  ```json
  "env": { "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN": "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" }
  ```
  Verify resolved keys before apply:
  ```bash
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run
  ```
  ## OAuth MCP (host-managed)
  After apply, open the target harness and complete OAuth there (Cursor MCP panel,
  `claude mcp`, Copilot `/mcp auth`, etc.). HarnessTap only writes server URL /
  transport: not OAuth tokens.
  ## Known gaps
  - **Shipped:** Cursor MCP scan/emit and HTTP `headers` round-trip (via `mcp-config-bridge`).
  - **OAuth sessions:** Browser OAuth tokens remain host-managed: environment switch does not re-auth for you.
  Remaining limitations: Known gaps and fix plan.
  Related: Portability limits,

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht environment create work --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit work --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-work
  ht environment create personal --from-plugin my-setup
  ht environment edit personal --secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:keychain:harnesstap/slack-personal
  ht environment use work
  ht profile use "global default" --reapply
  ht environment show work --plugin my-setup
  ht profile use "global default" --dry-run

Full doc: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/details/39-mcp-auth-and-environments.md
All scenarios: https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap/blob/main/docs/scenarios/scenarios.md

SCENARIO 40: USE PROJECT PROFILE CONFIG

Common · Shipped

  Use this when a repository ships `apm.yml` with named profiles
  so teammates can switch stacks without remembering plugin selectors.
  Create the file with `ht config init` (from local profile plugins) or copy a team template. See Project config for the `apm.yml` shape.
  ## Inspect the config
  ```bash
  ht config show
  ht config validate
  ht use --list
  ```
  `config validate` checks that inline profiles reference plugins defined in the
  same file and that default profile/environment keys resolve.
  ## Switch profiles
  ```bash
  ht use --profile dev
  ht use --profile prod --dry-run
  ht use                        # interactive picker when multiple profiles exist
  ```
  `ht use` resolves the profile source (local plugin, catalog selector, or inline
  plugin table), applies the profile to home harness paths, and optionally switches
  the active environment.
  For machine-wide presets outside a repo, use `profile use` instead
  (Scenario 36). For repo baselines without project
  config, use `apply` (Scenario 7).

TYPICAL COMMANDS

  ht config show
  ht config validate
  ht use --list
  ht use --profile dev
  ht use --profile prod --dry-run
  ht use                        # interactive picker when multiple profiles exist
